name: @prvtech/mcp

tools.name: get_me
tools.description:
Current session summary
Returns a slim view of the authenticated user — used by the layout header and the role-aware nav. Includes the user's MFA factor list when the request carries a cookie session; API-key callers always see `factors: []` (they bypass MFA by design). The `role` field is a UI hint only — every admin route re-queries it from the database via `requireAdminApi()`.
(GET /api/auth/me)

tools.name: list_bare_metal_catalog
tools.description:
List bare-metal plans
Returns bare-metal products available for purchase from the WHMCS "Bare Metal" group. Specs are extracted from the WHMCS product description (lines starting with `•`); category and slug come from inline `[category:xxx]` / `[slug:xxx]` markers (with keyword-based fallbacks). The response also includes a category summary so the UI can render filter chips.
(GET /api/bare-metal/catalog)

category.description: Filter to one category. Omit to return all plans (and the full category summary).

tools.name: list_bare_metal_servers
tools.description:
List your bare-metal servers
Returns the user's WHMCS services filtered to the Bare Metal product group, excluding Cancelled / Terminated rows.
(GET /api/bare-metal/servers)

tools.name: get_bare_metal_server
tools.description:
Get bare-metal server detail
Returns one bare-metal service. Verifies the WHMCS service belongs to the caller's WHMCS client.
(GET /api/bare-metal/servers/{id})

tools.name: delete_bare_metal_server
tools.description:
GET /api/bare-metal/servers/[id] — fetch single bare metal service
(DELETE /api/bare-metal/servers/{id})

tools.name: list_invoices
tools.description:
List your invoices
Returns the authenticated user's WHMCS invoices, newest first.
(GET /api/billing/invoices)

tools.name: get_invoice
tools.description:
Get invoice detail with line items
Returns one WHMCS invoice with line items, transactions, and the customer's billing address. For multi-month hosting lines a `pricingBreakdown` is computed so the UI can show the discount vs the monthly rate. Gateways are normalised — Eximbay / PayPal payments recorded by WHMCS under "banktransfer" are relabelled here using PRV's gateway tables.
(GET /api/billing/invoices/{id})

tools.name: get_billing_overview
tools.description:
Billing dashboard summary
Top-of-page billing card for the dashboard: account credit, default payment method, account status, member-since date, service counts, and the 5 most-due unpaid invoices. Each WHMCS source is cached separately (30-60s TTL) and keyed by WHMCS client id, so the call cost stays bounded under burst load.
(GET /api/billing/overview)

tools.name: list_billing_products
tools.description:
List products available for purchase
Returns WHMCS products eligible for new orders, excluding the Bare Metal group (use /api/bare-metal/catalog for those). Compute products are enriched with a `specs` block resolved from the matched VirtFusion package — first by `configoption1` (VirtFusion package id), then by name fallback. Cached for 30 seconds — short TTL because catalog price changes must reach the UI quickly.
(GET /api/billing/products)

tools.name: list_billing_services
tools.description:
List your active services
Returns the user's WHMCS services, paginated. Compute services are enriched with `projectId` + `projectName` (joined via `instance_provisions.whmcs_order_id` → `vf_server_id` → `project_instances`) and the linked `vfServerId` so the dashboard can deep-link without a second round trip. Cached server-side per (clientId, page, limit) for 30 seconds; invalidated after order writes.
(GET /api/billing/services)

tools.name: list_firewalls
tools.description:
List your firewall groups
Returns every firewall group owned by the user, enriched with `ruleCount` and `instanceCount`. When the optional `instance_id` query is supplied each group also gets `attachedToInstance: true|false` — the instance detail page uses this to render a single-roundtrip attachment matrix.
(GET /api/firewalls)

instance_id.description: VirtFusion server ID. When supplied, each returned group includes `attachedToInstance`.

tools.name: create_firewall
tools.description:
Create a firewall group
Creates an empty firewall group. The group is auto-assigned to the user's default project if `project_id` is omitted. Rules can be added afterwards via /api/firewalls/{id}/rules.
(POST /api/firewalls)

project_id.description: Falls back to the user's default project when omitted.

tools.name: get_firewall
tools.description:
Get a firewall group with its rules and attachments
Returns one firewall group's policy + all of its rules (ordered by priority) + the list of instance attachments.
(GET /api/firewalls/{id})

tools.name: update_firewall
tools.description:
GET /api/firewalls/[id] — get firewall group detail
(PATCH /api/firewalls/{id})

tools.name: delete_firewall
tools.description:
GET /api/firewalls/[id] — get firewall group detail
(DELETE /api/firewalls/{id})

tools.name: apply_firewall
tools.description:
Manually apply firewall rules
Pushes the group's current rules to vpc-agent on every attached instance's hypervisor. Most callers don't need this — every rule add / update / delete and every attachment change auto-enqueues the same apply job. Use this endpoint to force a re-apply (e.g. after rolling back a manual nftables tweak on a host). Returns per-instance success/failure so the UI can flag instances that didn't pick up the change.
(POST /api/firewalls/{id}/apply)

tools.name: attach_firewall
tools.description:
Attach an instance to a firewall group
Attaches one of your instances to this firewall group, then enqueues a durable `fw.apply` job to push the rules to the hypervisor. Each instance can only belong to one firewall group at a time — returns 409 if the instance is already attached elsewhere (the vpc-agent does a full nftables ruleset replace per VM-UUID, so multiple groups would silently overwrite each other). Verifies the caller owns BOTH the group and the target instance.
(POST /api/firewalls/{id}/attachments)

tools.name: detach_firewall
tools.description:
Detach an instance from a firewall group
Removes the firewall attachment, then best-effort calls vpc-agent to drop the per-VM nftables ruleset on the hypervisor. The DB delete is final from the user's perspective; vpc-agent failures are logged but don't surface in the response.
(DELETE /api/firewalls/{id}/attachments)

tools.name: create_firewall_rule
tools.description:
Add a rule to a firewall group
Inserts a new rule and enqueues a durable `fw.apply` job (5-second idempotency bucket) so the change is pushed to vpc-agent on every attached instance's hypervisor. `source` is restricted at the API layer to IPv4, IPv4 CIDR, or the literal `any` — free-form strings are rejected because the value flows verbatim into nftables.
(POST /api/firewalls/{id}/rules)

port_range.description: Single port ("80") or inclusive range ("8000-9000"). Each port must be 1-65535. Omit for icmp/all.

source.description: 'any', a bare IPv4, or an IPv4 CIDR.

tools.name: update_firewall_rule
tools.description:
Update a firewall rule
Updates fields on an existing rule (`rule_id` in body, not path). Only the fields you include are changed. After the DB write, a durable `fw.apply` job is enqueued (5s idempotency bucket) to push the new ruleset to all attached instances. `source` accepts only `any`, IPv4, or IPv4 CIDR — free-form strings are rejected because the value flows verbatim into nftables.
(PATCH /api/firewalls/{id}/rules)

tools.name: delete_firewall_rule
tools.description:
Delete a firewall rule
Removes the rule from the group (`rule_id` in body, not path), then enqueues a durable `fw.apply` job (5s idempotency bucket) to push the updated ruleset to all attached instances. Returns 404 when the rule does not belong to this group.
(DELETE /api/firewalls/{id}/rules)

tools.name: list_instances
tools.description:
List your VPS instances
Returns every instance owned by the authenticated user, with pagination. Owner is determined by the user's Supabase id → `profiles.virtfusion_user_id` mapping.
(GET /api/instances)

tools.name: get_instance
tools.description:
Get a single VPS instance
Returns the full detail view for one instance you own — power state, hardware spec, attached IPs, region label, and a best-effort monthly cost (resolved through WHMCS; null on lookup failure).
(GET /api/instances/{id})

tools.name: delete_instance
tools.description:
Destroy a VPS instance
Permanently destroys the instance in VirtFusion and cleans up its Supabase rows (project link, VPC membership, firewall attachments). Provision records are soft-deleted (status = `failed`) so the audit trail survives. This is irreversible — all data on the VM is lost.
(DELETE /api/instances/{id})

tools.name: get_instance_console
tools.description:
Get a noVNC console URL
Asks VirtFusion to enable VNC for the instance and returns a short-lived WebSocket URL + one-time password that noVNC can connect to. The session is single-use; refresh this endpoint to start a new console session.
(GET /api/instances/{id}/console)

tools.name: reset_instance_password
tools.description:
Change root password on a VPS
Sets a new root password on the running instance over SSH. The route looks up the instance's primary IPv4, verifies the captured-at-provisioning host fingerprint to refuse swapped/hijacked hosts, then runs `chpasswd` over a stdin pipe (no password on the command line, no shell quoting). Refuses if the instance is on hold or has no primary IPv4.
(POST /api/instances/{id}/password)

password.description: New root password. Pass it as plain text — the route never logs or persists it.

tools.name: power_instance
tools.description:
Power action on a VPS
Sends a power command to one of your instances. `kill` is a hard power-off — use it only when the VM is unresponsive (in-flight writes may be lost). `start` / `restart` automatically re-attach the instance to its VPC networks and re-apply the IP configuration after boot.
(POST /api/instances/{id}/power)

action.description: start = boot, stop = graceful shutdown, restart = reboot, kill = force power off (data may be lost)

tools.name: get_instance_project
tools.description:
Get the project an instance belongs to
Returns the project the instance is assigned to (via `project_instances`). Returns `{ project_id: null, project: null }` when the instance is unassigned.
(GET /api/instances/{id}/project)

tools.name: get_instance_provision
tools.description:
get provision info (package_id etc.)
GET /api/instances/[id]/provision — get provision info (package_id etc.)
(GET /api/instances/{id}/provision)

tools.name: rebuild_instance
tools.description:
Reinstall the OS on a VPS
Triggers a fresh OS install on the existing instance. Destroys all data on the disk. The rebuild is rejected (409) if the VM is currently in `building` / `queued` / `rebuilding` state to avoid undefined post-setup state. A per-server in-process lock additionally serialises rapid retries.
(POST /api/instances/{id}/rebuild)

sshKeys.description: VirtFusion SSH key IDs to inject during the build.

tools.name: resize_instance
tools.description:
Change package (resize) a VPS
Creates a WHMCS upgrade order + invoice for moving the instance to a new product (different CPU/RAM/disk). Does NOT auto-settle the invoice — the customer must pay it via the normal billing path; the WHMCS VirtFusion module then applies the upgrade. Serialised by an in-process per-server lock plus a 24h cross-process "already pending upgrade" check to prevent double-billing on rapid retries.
(POST /api/instances/{id}/resize)

productId.description: WHMCS product ID of the new package. Get this from /api/billing/products.

tools.name: get_instance_stats
tools.description:
Current resource usage for a VPS
Returns the latest CPU / memory / disk / network sample for one instance. CPU is computed as the delta between two scrapes of the cumulative `virtfusion_vm_cpu_time_nanos` counter, so the first call after process start may return 0%. All values fall back to 0 when the Prometheus exporter is offline (an observability event is emitted server-side).
(GET /api/instances/{id}/stats)

tools.name: get_instance_traffic_history
tools.description:
Bandwidth history for a VPS
Returns time-series RX / TX rate (bytes per second) for one instance over a chosen window. Suitable for plotting; step size is auto-chosen to keep each series around 150-300 points.

Sources from the Prometheus exporter via the VM → device mapping. Returns empty series when the VM has no recorded devices (newly built, exporter just restarted).
(GET /api/instances/{id}/traffic-history)

tools.name: deploy_instance
tools.description:
Create (deploy) a new VPS instance
Starts a new instance provisioning. The wizard normally calls this after the user has settled an Eximbay or PayPal payment; the payment context is passed as `paymentOrderId` + `paymentGateway` to make the call idempotent across retries / refreshes. Without a gateway, a deploy whose price is fully covered by `useCredit` (account balance) and/or `promoCode` provisions directly — the headless path for API-key / MCP clients with a funded balance. Returns a `provisionId` you can poll via /api/instances/provisions/{id} until status becomes `complete`.

This endpoint always returns HTTP 200 (even on validation / upstream errors) — inspect the JSON body's `error` field to detect failure. The unusual envelope dodges Cloudflare's 5xx body rewrite.
(POST /api/instances/deploy)

whmcsProductId.description: WHMCS product ID — the package the user is buying.

osId.description: VirtFusion OS template ID from /api/os-templates (0 means "not set").

rootPassword.description: Encrypted at rest in instance_provisions; decrypted by the post-build webhook to set the password over SSH.

vpcId.description: Attach to this VPC after build.

firewallGroupId.description: Attach this firewall group after build.

paymentOrderId.description: Order ID from a prior gateway payment (Eximbay/PayPal). Required for the paid web-checkout flow.

useCredit.description: WHMCS account-credit amount to apply, in the client's billing currency. Enables a GATEWAY-FREE deploy: when `useCredit` (+ optional `promoCode`) covers the plan price exactly, the server — which re-reads the live balance and recomputes, refusing unless the remaining total is 0 — provisions without a payment redirect. This is the path an API-key / MCP client uses to deploy headlessly from a funded balance.

promoCode.description: Optional WHMCS promotion code, validated server-side at AddOrder time. Combines with `useCredit` for a fully-covered, gateway-free deploy.

tools.name: get_provision
tools.description:
Get provisioning status
Poll this endpoint after /api/instances/deploy until `status` is `complete` (or `failed`). The wizard polls every 2-3 seconds; the row exists in Supabase from the moment deploy returns, even before WHMCS / VirtFusion finish.
(GET /api/instances/provisions/{id})

tools.name: list_ip_addresses
tools.description:
List IP addresses across your instances
Walks every instance in the user's VirtFusion account, extracts each NIC's IPv4 / IPv6 addresses, and enriches them with the user's reservation metadata (label, reverse DNS).
(GET /api/ip-addresses)

tools.name: reserve_ip_addresses
tools.description:
Reserve additional IPv4 addresses on a server
Allocates additional IPv4 addresses on the server's primary interface via VirtFusion's `ipv4Qty` endpoint, then stores reservation metadata (label, server name) in Supabase. The allocated addresses are returned in `data.addresses` so the UI can show them immediately. Quantity is capped at 10 per call.
(POST /api/ip-addresses)

tools.name: release_ip_addresses
tools.description:
Release an IP address
Removes an IPv4 address from the server via VirtFusion and deletes the matching reservation row from Supabase. Both `serverId` and `address` are sent in the request body. Returns `{ released: true }` on success.
(DELETE /api/ip-addresses)

tools.name: list_notifications
tools.description:
List in-app notifications
Returns the authenticated user's notifications, newest first, plus an `unreadCount` for the bell badge. The response is browser-cacheable for 10 seconds (private) to let multiple components on the same page share a single fetch.
(GET /api/notifications)

unread.description: Set to `true` to return only unread notifications. The `unreadCount` is still computed across the user's full inbox.

tools.name: mark_notifications_read
tools.description:
Mark notifications as read
Marks notifications as read. Pass `all: true` to mark every unread notification as read in one call, or `ids: [...]` to mark specific notifications. Always returns `{ success: true }` even when no rows matched.
(PATCH /api/notifications)

ids.description: Specific notification ids to mark read. Mutually exclusive with `all` (if both are present, `all` wins).

all.description: Mark every unread notification as read.

tools.name: list_os_templates
tools.description:
List installable OS templates
Returns OS template groups (e.g. "Ubuntu", "Debian") with their concrete installable images. Pass `templates[].id` as `osId` in /api/instances/deploy or `operatingSystemId` in /api/instances/{id}/rebuild. Cached for 5 minutes — operator-managed list that rarely changes.
(GET /api/os-templates)

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description:
avatar feature removed (slowloris-style upload abuse +
avatar feature removed (slowloris-style upload abuse +
Storage egress amplification). The `avatar_url` column is left in
the DB but never read or written by the application.
(GET /api/profile)

tools.name: update_profile
tools.description:
Update your profile
Updates editable profile fields. Changing `phone` resets `phone_verified` to false in both `profiles` and the Supabase JWT's `user_metadata` so the proxy gate immediately starts blocking until the new number is re-verified. Updating `firstName` or `lastName` recomputes `display_name`.
(PATCH /api/profile)

phone.description: Changing this resets phone_verified to false.

tools.name: get_notification_preferences
tools.description:
Get notification preferences
Returns the per-channel notification opt-ins for the authenticated user. Empty object `{}` is returned when no preferences have been saved yet (treat all channels as enabled by default in the UI).
(GET /api/profile/notifications)

tools.name: update_notification_preferences
tools.description:
Update notification preferences
Replaces the user's notification preferences. Every channel is required — partial updates are not supported (the route validates the full object).
(PATCH /api/profile/notifications)

security.description: Login alerts, MFA changes, password resets, etc.

infrastructure.description: Provisioning events, region maintenance, instance state changes.

announcements.description: Product changelog, new features, planned downtime.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description:
List your projects
Returns every project owned by the user, with inline `resourceCounts` (instances / VPCs / firewall groups) to avoid an N+1 fetch from the dashboard.
(GET /api/projects)

tools.name: create_project
tools.description:
Create a project
Creates a new project to group instances, VPCs, and firewall groups. The first project on the account is auto-flagged as default.
(POST /api/projects)

tools.name: get_project
tools.description:
Get project detail
Returns one project with its attached VPCs, firewall groups, and instances inlined. Instances are merged from two sources: direct `project_instances` rows and indirect `vpc_members` rows for VPCs that belong to this project (deduplicated by instance id).
(GET /api/projects/{id})

tools.name: update_project
tools.description:
Update a project
Updates the project's name or description. The default project can be renamed but not unflagged.
(PATCH /api/projects/{id})

tools.name: delete_project
tools.description:
Delete a project
Deletes the project. Refuses (409) when the project has attached VPCs / firewall groups / instances unless `?force=1` is passed — passing `force` deliberately orphans those resources (VPCs and firewall groups have their `project_id` set to NULL; project_instances rows are removed). The default project cannot be deleted (returns 400). Both refusal and deletion are audited.
(DELETE /api/projects/{id})

force.description: Pass `1` to delete the project and orphan its attached resources. Without it the request is refused (409) when attachments exist.

tools.name: list_project_available_resources
tools.description:
List resources eligible to attach to a project
Returns VPCs, firewall groups, and VirtFusion instances the user owns that are NOT already in this project (or are unassigned). Used by the project detail page's "Add resource" picker so the UI doesn't show items that are already attached. Falls back to an empty `instances` array when VirtFusion is unreachable — the rest of the response still resolves.
(GET /api/projects/{id}/available-resources)

tools.name: add_instance_to_project
tools.description:
Add an instance to a project
Links one of your VirtFusion instances to this project (idempotent — re-adding the same instance is a no-op). Verifies the caller owns BOTH the project and the target instance.
(POST /api/projects/{id}/instances)

tools.name: remove_instance_from_project
tools.description:
Remove an instance from a project
Removes the project link for the instance. The `instance_id` is sent in the request body, not the path. Returns success even when the link did not exist.
(DELETE /api/projects/{id}/instances)

tools.name: manage_project_resources
tools.description:
Add / remove / transfer a resource to or from a project
Single mutation endpoint for changing a resource's project assignment. `add` sets `project_id` to this project; `remove` clears it; `transfer` moves it to `targetProjectId` (which must also be owned by the caller). `type` selects the table (`vpc` → `vpc_networks`, `firewall` → `firewall_groups`).
(POST /api/projects/{id}/resources)

targetProjectId.description: Required when `action` is `transfer`. Must be a project owned by the caller.

tools.name: list_regions
tools.description:
List available compute regions
Returns the VirtFusion hypervisor groups the user can target when deploying. Cached for 10 minutes globally — the list changes at most weekly.
(GET /api/regions)

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Cross-resource search
Searches projects (Supabase ILIKE), instances (VirtFusion server list filtered by hostname / name / IP / id), and invoices (WHMCS most-recent 100 filtered by number / total). Each source has a soft 4s timeout and runs in parallel — one slow upstream cannot block the rest. `truncated.<source>: true` indicates more matches exist than the per-source limit (5).
(GET /api/search)

q.description: Search query. Trimmed and lowercased before matching; capped at 100 chars.

tools.name: list_ssh_keys
tools.description:
List your SSH keys
Returns SSH public keys stored in VirtFusion for the user's account.
(GET /api/ssh-keys)

tools.name: create_ssh_key
tools.description:
Register an SSH public key
Stores a new OpenSSH-format public key against the user's VirtFusion account. The key can then be selected during instance deploy / rebuild to authorise root access on first boot.

Keys are validated against a strict regex (ssh-rsa / ssh-ed25519 / ssh-dss / ecdsa-sha2-* / sk-*) and capped at 8 KB — pass the `id` ssh-keygen would print, not a private key.
(POST /api/ssh-keys)

publicKey.description: OpenSSH-format public key (ssh-rsa / ssh-ed25519 / ecdsa-sha2-* / sk-*).

tools.name: delete_ssh_key
tools.description:
Delete an SSH key
Removes a stored SSH public key from VirtFusion. The key id is sent in the request body (not the path). Verifies the key belongs to the caller before deletion. Audited as `ssh_key.delete` in the user's security activity timeline.
(DELETE /api/ssh-keys)

tools.name: list_support_departments
tools.description:
List support ticket departments
Returns WHMCS support departments that can receive a new ticket. Pass `id` as `deptid` when calling POST /api/support/tickets.
(GET /api/support/departments)

tools.name: list_support_tickets
tools.description:
List your support tickets
Returns the user's WHMCS support tickets, paginated. The response is cached server-side per (clientId, page, limit, status) for 60 seconds — open / close events are rare and the cache is invalidated immediately when the same user opens a new ticket via POST.
(GET /api/support/tickets)

tools.name: create_support_ticket
tools.description:
Open a new support ticket
Creates a new ticket in WHMCS for the calling user. Rate-limited to 5 tickets per 5 minutes per user to keep the support queue from being flooded by automation. Pick `deptid` from /api/support/departments.
(POST /api/support/tickets)

message.example: Hi, my instance web-prod-1 stopped responding to SSH about 20 minutes ago…

tools.name: get_support_ticket
tools.description:
Get a support ticket with replies
Returns one ticket with its full reply chain (oldest first). Verifies the ticket belongs to the calling user via the WHMCS client id link.
(GET /api/support/tickets/{id})

id.description: WHMCS ticket ID (numeric, not the TKT- string).

tools.name: reply_support_ticket
tools.description:
Reply to a support ticket
Adds a reply (from the user's side) to an existing ticket. Verifies ticket ownership before posting. Rate-limited to 10 replies per minute per user to keep the SMTP queue safe.
(POST /api/support/tickets/{id}/reply)

message.example: Thanks — yes, please proceed with the rebuild.

tools.name: list_vpc_networks
tools.description:
List your VPC networks
Lists overlay VPC networks visible to the authenticated user, optionally scoped to a project.
(GET /api/vpc-networks)

project_id.description: Filter to a specific project. Omit to return networks across all your projects.

tools.name: create_vpc_network
tools.description:
Create a VPC network
Allocates a fresh VXLAN VNI and creates the overlay network on the chosen region's hypervisor. The first member instance attached to this VPC triggers per-host nftables rules via the vpc-agent.
(POST /api/vpc-networks)

tools.name: get_vpc_network
tools.description:
Get VPC network detail
Returns one VPC with its members inlined and a friendly `region_label` resolved from VirtFusion's hypervisor groups.
(GET /api/vpc-networks/{id})

tools.name: update_vpc_network
tools.description:
GET /api/vpc-networks/[id] — get VPC detail
(PATCH /api/vpc-networks/{id})

tools.name: delete_vpc_network
tools.description:
Delete a VPC network
Removes the VPC from Supabase, then enqueues a `vpc.cleanup` background job to tear down the bridge / VXLAN on the hypervisor. The DB delete is final from the user's perspective; transient vpc-agent errors show up as failed jobs in /admin-jobs and do not block the response. Returns 409 if any instances are still attached — detach members first.
(DELETE /api/vpc-networks/{id})

tools.name: list_vpc_network_members
tools.description:
List VPC members
Returns all instances currently attached to the VPC, with their private IPs inside the overlay.
(GET /api/vpc-networks/{id}/members)

tools.name: attach_vpc_member
tools.description:
Attach an instance to the VPC
Adds the named instance as a member of this VPC. Auto-assigns a free `.2`-onward private IP from the VPC's CIDR block if `private_ip` is not provided. Each instance can only belong to one VPC at a time — returns 409 if the target instance is already attached elsewhere. After the DB row is created the route calls vpc-agent to attach the NIC on the hypervisor and (best-effort) SSHs into the VM to bring up the new interface.
(POST /api/vpc-networks/{id}/members)

tools.name: detach_vpc_member
tools.description:
Detach an instance from the VPC
Removes the instance from this VPC. The DB row is removed immediately; a durable `vpc.cleanup` job is enqueued (5s idempotency bucket) to detach the NIC on the hypervisor via vpc-agent. Verifies the caller owns BOTH the VPC and the target instance — without the latter, owning any VPC was previously enough to detach another tenant's instance.
(DELETE /api/vpc-networks/{id}/members)

tools.name: suggest_vpc_cidr
tools.description:
GET /api/vpc-networks/suggest-cidr
(GET /api/vpc-networks/suggest-cidr)
